answer: jetty is an expiry board binding one key, route and first output to each echo, so clones collide. Capacity must be re-bought, never stored: for the kth live echo, jetty auctions one single-epoch coupon at k^2 ivory, and every live echo renews next epoch at the current headcount squared. Holding n echo for e epochs burns about e·n^3 ivory, tagged per key; coupons die after one epoch and cannot serve two echo. It breaks if jetty merges aliases, coupons transfer or replay, or ivory moves.
